The Stoics (network name; Cato is the first of three)

summary: Proposed ~600 MW hyperscale AI/cloud data centre campus of around £5bn on farmland north-west of Auchtertool village, Fife, promoted by ILI Group through SPV ILI Cato Limited. A planning permission in principle application (26/01243/PPP) was validated by Fife Council on 21 May 2026 for a campus of six to seven data hall buildings up to 35 m high (~280,000 m2 of buildings), gatehouses, substations and infrastructure. Fife Council's 1 April 2026 screening opinion said EIA was not required, but Scottish Ministers subsequently considered the proposal through DPEA case EIA-250-002 and directed on 17 August 2026 that an EIA is required. The first of ILI's three planned 'Stoics' data centres (with Rufus, East Ayrshire, and Aurelius, North Lanarkshire). The application drew over 1,200 published objections and reportedly 14,000-16,000 total representations, plus a SEPA holding objection on flooding.
maturity_explanation: Formal planning permission in principle application 26/01243/PPP was validated by Fife Council on 21 May 2026 and remains undetermined. It was preceded by PAN 25/00552/PAN and council EIA screening 25/03079/SCR. Scottish Ministers' later screening direction EIA-250-002, issued 17 August 2026, requires an Environmental Impact Assessment for the proposal.
anticipated_operational_date: Phased over roughly five years from a 2027 start (developer); a three-year build programme was also reported

phases.phase_name: Phased build-out of six identical-footprint data hall buildings
phases.description: The campus is designed as six separate buildings with identical footprints to enable phased construction (some reporting says up to seven buildings); energy use rising from ~400 GWh/yr in early phases to a possible ~4,000 GWh/yr at full build-out.

latest_development.headline: Scottish Ministers direct that an Environmental Impact Assessment is required for application 26/01243/PPP (DPEA EIA-250-002), reversing the practical effect of Fife Council's earlier no-EIA screening opinion
